title: Had It Been So: Past Conditions Without Si

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si hubiera* + past participle from B1 Unit 35, and from B2 Unit 10 you know that *hubiera* + participle can open a sentence in place of *si* (*Hubiera salido antes, habría llegado*), and that *aunque* or *aun cuando* + *hubiera* + participle means "even if … had …". The history of the Pacific Alliance gives you days and events to imagine differently.

items.spanish: Hubiera estado en Lima el 28 de abril de 2011, habría visto la firma de la Declaración de Lima.
items.english: Had I been in Lima on 28 April 2011, I would have seen the signing of the Lima Declaration.

items.spanish: Hubiéramos viajado a Lima en abril de 2011, habríamos visto a los presidentes de los cuatro países.
items.english: Had we travelled to Lima in April 2011, we would have seen the presidents of the four countries.

items.spanish: Aun cuando México no se hubiera unido al MILA en 2014, el mercado habría seguido con tres bolsas.
items.english: Even if Mexico had not joined MILA in 2014, the market would have gone on with three stock exchanges.

sections.content: Only *hubiera* (or *hubiese*) + participle can open the sentence in place of *si*, and the result clause uses *habría* + participle. Do not put *habré* or a past tense in its place.
